title: Ashawagh
summary: Ashawagh is a Montaukett placename and settlement locality at Hand's Creek, near Three Mile Harbor in East Hampton. It as a locality where shell heaps, arrow points, and pottery fragments marked an Indigenous village site. The name is interpreted as a place between, referring to land between the creek branches.
address_label: Hand's Creek / Three Mile Harbor, East Hampton, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Existing point retained for the Hand's Creek / Three Mile Harbor Ashawagh locality; approximate but strongly supported by source descriptions.
why_this_matters: Ashawagh preserves a Montaukett placename for a settlement locality at Hand's Creek near Three Mile Harbor, interpreted as a place between or in the middle. That meaning fits a creek-and-harbor landscape where position, water access, fishing, shellfish, and travel all mattered. East Hampton's waterways remain part of continuing Montaukett geography and memory, not only scenic views or modern place names.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Ashshowale, Ashawagk, Ashwagh, Ashawog, Assawog, and Nashaway. The name is interpreted as a place between, referring to land between the forks or branches of the creek.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names tell us a lot about our nation’s past.”

— Valerie Fridland, What’s in a Name? The Hidden History Behind Place Names (2024), Key points, first bullet
colonial_description_content:
James Truslow Adams, in his History of The Town of Southampton [1. James Truslow Adams, History of the Town of Southampton (East of Canoe Place), 1918 pp. 29], writes;
The Montauks had an extensive settlement of "half a hundred" wigwams on the west side of Three Mile Harbor.
whereintheworld_content: Ashawagh connects a named Montaukett place with settlement, wetland meadows, shell working, and continued memory of Hand's Creek. It is also a reminder to distinguish nearby place names: Ashawagh names the settlement/locality, while Copeces refers more broadly to the creek setting.
